heading: Matching
text:
### Matching [LTSL.8.4]

A head with slot arguments matches by partial (subset) equality; a slot the head
does not name is free on the observed fact. An `emitted` head
matches either by slot arguments or by a binding and a `where` predicate
([LTSL.4.2]), never by both: a head carrying both does not parse ([LGRA.21.1]),
and an author states a condition on a slot inside the predicate.

A `published` head matches by slot arguments alone. The compiler must refuse a
`where` predicate on a `published` head, with or without `never`, with
`DS_VALIDATE_TEST_PUBLISHED_WHERE`: the predicate is a rule over working memory
([RTIM.14.11]), and a `publish` puts nothing there ([LTIE.4.3]).

The `OracleEmit` atom carries `has_where`, and an atom that
carries it carries no `slot_match` ([RDSC.7.1]); the predicate itself is realized as a
compiler-synthesized internal rule and the oracle is bound to it by name, not by
an expression reference ([RTIM.14.11]). A `retracted` head
matches by slot-subset equality only — its `OracleRetract` atom carries no `where`. The
remaining heads carry no slot arguments and match by their identifying key: `called`
by service and optional correlation, `cached` by key and
optional value, and `logged` by level and optional substring
([LTSL.8.2]). Call-argument equality is keyed on the `for call` response
stub ([LTSL.7.2]), not on the `called` oracle head.
